passages.text: For if you become occupied with the cares of ordinary life, you will ensnare both yourself and your hearers. For because your occupations leave you unable to furnish what is beneficial as provisions, you will be punished for not teaching what is beneficial, while those who did not learn will perish, ignorance being the cause. Therefore, give them your undistracted time and preside over them, so that at the right time you may provide words capable of saving them. And so let them heed you, knowing that whatever the ambassador of the truth binds on earth has also been bound in heaven, and whatever he looses has been loosed. You, however, will bind what must be bound and loose what must be loosed. And as for the matters concerning you, the presiding officer, these are they, along with things like them.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: βιωτικαῖς μερίμναις ἀσχοληθῇς
lexical_decisions.chosen: become occupied with the cares of ordinary life
lexical_decisions.rationale: βιωτικός concerns ordinary worldly life, while ἀσχολέομαι emphasizes being occupied and deprived of leisure.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τὰ γὰρ συμφέροντα ἐφοδιάζειν
lexical_decisions.chosen: to furnish what is beneficial as provisions
lexical_decisions.rationale: ἐφοδιάζω evokes supplying provisions or equipping someone for a journey.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: εὐσχολῶν προκαθέσθητι
lexical_decisions.chosen: give them your undistracted time and preside over them
lexical_decisions.rationale: εὐσχολέω contrasts with prior preoccupation, while προκαθέζομαι denotes taking the leading or presiding position.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ὁ τῆς ἀληθείας πρεσβευτὴς ὃ ἂν δήσῃ ἐπὶ γῆς, δέδεται καὶ ἐν οὐρανῷ
lexical_decisions.chosen: whatever the ambassador of the truth binds on earth has also been bound in heaven
lexical_decisions.rationale: πρεσβευτής denotes an authorized envoy, and the Greek perfect is retained rather than harmonized with a familiar future-tense rendering.

source_issues.source_quote: οἱ δὲ μὴ μαθόντες ἀγνοίας αἰτία ἀπολοῦνται
source_issues.issue: The printed nominative αἰτία is syntactically abrupt. The translation understands it parenthetically as “ignorance being the cause”; a causal dative is a possible conjecture.
source_issues.proposed_reading: οἱ δὲ μὴ μαθόντες ἀγνοίας αἰτίᾳ ἀπολοῦνται

source_issues.issue: The printed full stop interrupts the construction and separates μὲν from the phrase it appears to qualify. The translation reads the words as continuous in sense without treating the supplied punctuation as an OCR error.

passages.text: But let the duties concerning the elders be these: above all, let them quickly join the young in marriage, forestalling the snares of youthful desire. But let them not neglect marriage even for those already old, for in some people desire remains vigorous even after they have grown old. Therefore, so that sexual immorality may not gain ground against you and cast the same plague into your midst, take precautions beforehand and investigate whether the fire of adultery may be springing up secretly among you. For adultery is exceedingly terrible—so much so that it holds second place in punishment, since first place is awarded to those who are in error, even if they are chaste. Therefore, as elders of the church, train Christ’s bride in chastity (and by “bride” I mean the corporate body of the church). For if she is found chaste by the bridegroom king, she will obtain the greatest honor, and you, as those invited to the wedding, will enjoy great rejoicing. But if she is discovered to have sinned, she will be cast out, and you will pay the penalty if perhaps the sin came about through your neglect.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: πρὸ πάντων τοὺς νέους πρὸς γάμον ζευγνύτωσαν ἐν τάχει
lexical_decisions.chosen: above all, let them quickly join the young in marriage
lexical_decisions.rationale: ζευγνύω literally joins or yokes together and here refers to arranging marriage.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τῆς νεαζούσης ἐπιθυμίας τὰ παγιδεύματα
lexical_decisions.chosen: the snares of youthful desire
lexical_decisions.rationale: The rendering preserves the trapping image of παγίδευμα and treats νεάζουσα as characterizing desire associated with youth.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἡ πορνεία νομὴν λαβοῦσα καθ’ ὑμῶν
lexical_decisions.chosen: sexual immorality may not gain ground against you
lexical_decisions.rationale: νομὴν λαμβάνειν can describe spreading or gaining range, especially of disease or fire.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τοσοῦτον ὅσον τὰ δευτερεῖα ἔχειν αὐτὴν τῆς κολάσεως
lexical_decisions.chosen: so much so that it holds second place in punishment
lexical_decisions.rationale: δευτερεῖα denotes second rank or second prize; the ranking image is retained.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἐπεὶ τὰ πρωτεῖα τοῖς ἐν πλάνῃ οὖσιν ἀποδίδοται, κἂν σωφρονῶσιν
lexical_decisions.chosen: since first place is awarded to those who are in error, even if they are chaste
lexical_decisions.rationale: πλάνη may denote doctrinal or moral error, but the text does not specify further; the surprising concession about chastity is preserved.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: νύμφην δὲ λέγω τῆς ἐκκλησίας τὸ σύστημα
lexical_decisions.chosen: and by “bride” I mean the corporate body of the church
lexical_decisions.rationale: σύστημα denotes an organized whole or collective body.

passages.text: Therefore, above all, concern yourselves with chastity, for sexual immorality has been decreed exceedingly grave in God’s sight. There are many kinds of sexual immorality, as Clement himself will also explain to you. But the first is adultery: a man’s not having relations only with his own wife, and a woman’s not having relations only with her own husband. If someone is chaste, he can also become benevolent, for which reason he will obtain eternal mercy. Just as adultery is a great evil, so benevolence is the greatest good. Therefore love all your brothers with reverent and merciful eyes, doing for orphans what parents do and for widows what husbands do, providing sustenance with complete gladness, marriages for those in their prime, and, for those among them without a trade, devising through occupations the means of necessary sustenance: work for a craftsperson, mercy for one who is inactive.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: λίαν γὰρ παρὰ τῷ θεῷ χαλεπὴ ὥρισται ἡ πορνεία
lexical_decisions.chosen: sexual immorality has been decreed exceedingly grave in God’s sight
lexical_decisions.rationale: ὁρίζω indicates authoritative determination, while χαλεπή here describes severity or gravity.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: πορνείας δὲ εἴδη πολλά, ὡς καὶ αὐτὸς Κλήμης ὑμῖν διηγήσεται
lexical_decisions.chosen: There are many kinds of sexual immorality, as Clement himself will also explain to you
lexical_decisions.rationale: The translation preserves καί, which marks Clement himself as also supplying the promised explanation.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: πλὴν πρώτη μοιχεία ἐστὶν
lexical_decisions.chosen: But the first is adultery
lexical_decisions.rationale: πρώτη is understood as the first of the previously mentioned kinds, without adding that it is necessarily the worst.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τὸ ἄνδρα μὴ ἰδίᾳ μόνῃ χρήσασθαι γυναικὶ καὶ γυναῖκα μὴ ἰδίῳ μόνῳ χρήσασθαι ἀνδρί
lexical_decisions.chosen: a man’s not having relations only with his own wife, and a woman’s not having relations only with her own husband
lexical_decisions.rationale: χρῆσθαι with a spouse in this context refers to sexual or marital relations; a literal rendering with “use” would mislead.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἐὰν σώφρων ᾖ τις, καὶ φιλάνθρωπος γενέσθαι δύναται
lexical_decisions.chosen: If someone is chaste, he can also become benevolent
lexical_decisions.rationale: φιλάνθρωπος denotes humane, generous concern for others and is distinguished from the later command ἀγαπᾶτε, rendered “love.”

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τοῖς αὐτῶν ἀτέχνοις διὰ τῶν ἐπιτηδευμάτων ἐννοούμενοι τὰς προφάσεις τῆς ἀναγκαίας τροφῆς
lexical_decisions.chosen: for those among them without a trade, devising through occupations the means of necessary sustenance
lexical_decisions.rationale: ἀτέχνοις is taken as “unskilled” or “without a trade,” while προφάσεις denotes practical occasions or means in this context.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τεχνίτῃ ἔργον, ἀδρανεῖ ἔλεος
lexical_decisions.chosen: work for a craftsperson, mercy for one who is inactive
lexical_decisions.rationale: The compressed contrast assigns work to the craftsperson and charitable aid to the inactive person; ἀδρανής may imply idleness, inactivity, or inability to work.

passages.text: I know that you will do these things if you establish love in your mind. There is one sufficient occasion for its entry: the common sharing of salt. Therefore make every effort to dine with one another as often as you can, so that you do not barter it away; for it is the cause of doing good, and doing good is the cause of salvation. All of you, then, make your means of life common to everyone who is a brother according to God, knowing that by giving temporary things you will receive eternal things. All the more, feed the hungry and provide drink to the thirsty, clothing to the naked; visit the sick; make yourselves present to those in prison and help them as you can; receive strangers into your own homes with complete eagerness. But, so that I do not speak item by item, benevolence will teach you to do every good thing, just as misanthropy points out the practice of evil to those who do not wish to be saved.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: μία τις ἐστὶν ἱκανὴ πρόφασις, ἡ κοινὴ τῶν ἁλῶν μετάληψις
lexical_decisions.chosen: There is one sufficient occasion for its entry: the common sharing of salt
lexical_decisions.rationale: πρόφασις here denotes an occasion or means, while the specific salt image evokes shared food and table fellowship.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: σπουδάζετε πυκνότερον συνέστιοι ἀλλήλων γίνεσθαι ὡς δύνασθε
lexical_decisions.chosen: make every effort to dine with one another as often as you can
lexical_decisions.rationale: σύνεστιος describes sharing a table or household meal, and πυκνότερον indicates increased frequency.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ὅπως αὐτὴν μὴ ἀπεμπολήσητε
lexical_decisions.chosen: so that you do not barter it away
lexical_decisions.rationale: The pronoun refers to love, and ἀπεμπολέω supplies a commercial image of selling or trading something away.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: κοινοὺς οὖν πάντες πᾶσιν τοῖς κατὰ θεὸν ἀδελφοῖς τοὺς ἑαυτῶν παρέχετε βίους
lexical_decisions.chosen: All of you, then, make your means of life common to everyone who is a brother according to God
lexical_decisions.rationale: βίος can denote life, livelihood, or material means; the giving context favors “means of life” while retaining more breadth than “money.”

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τοῖς ἐν φυλακαῖς ἐπιφαινόμενοι ὡς δύνασθε βοηθεῖτε
lexical_decisions.chosen: make yourselves present to those in prison and help them as you can
lexical_decisions.rationale: ἐπιφαίνομαι literally denotes appearing or making oneself visible, here in the practical sense of visiting or being present.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἵνα μὴ τὸ κατ᾽ εἶδος λέγω
lexical_decisions.chosen: so that I do not speak item by item
lexical_decisions.rationale: κατ᾽ εἶδος here means treating each matter separately by kind or category.

source_issues.issue: The printed middle dot separates παρέχετε from ποτόν even though “drink” naturally serves as its object. The translation construes them together while disclosing the punctuation.

passages.text: Brothers who have disputes must not be judged before the authorities, but must in every way be brought to agreement by the elders of the church, readily obeying them. Moreover, flee greed, since under the pretext of temporary gain it can deprive you of eternal good things. Do you carefully observe fair balances, measures, weights, and the just standards of the various localities? Act honorably with regard to deposits entrusted to you. Moreover, you will persevere in doing these and similar things to the end if you keep in your hearts an inseparable remembrance of the judgment that comes from God. For who could sin while fully convinced that a judgment from the righteous God—who only for now is patient and good—has been appointed to take place at life’s end, so that the good may thereafter enjoy the inexpressible good things everlastingly, while those found to be sinners will, as evil people, receive inexpressible punishment throughout the age? And as for these things being so, if the prophet of the truth had not stated under oath that they would be, it might perhaps have been reasonable to doubt.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: οἱ πράγματα ἔχοντες ἀδελφοὶ
lexical_decisions.chosen: Brothers who have disputes
lexical_decisions.rationale: πράγματα ἔχειν in this legal setting refers to having cases, grievances, or disputes.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ὑπὸ τῶν τῆς ἐκκλησίας πρεσβυτέρων συμβιβαζέσθωσαν παντὶ τρόπῳ
lexical_decisions.chosen: must in every way be brought to agreement by the elders of the church
lexical_decisions.rationale: συμβιβάζω here concerns reconciling the parties or settling their dispute.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ζυγά, μέτρα, σταθμία, τὰ τῶντόπων δίκαια ἐπιμελῶς φυλάσσετε;
lexical_decisions.chosen: Do you carefully observe fair balances, measures, weights, and the just standards of the various localities?
lexical_decisions.rationale: The supplied punctuation is represented as a question; φυλάσσετε can formally be either indicative or imperative.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: πρὸς τὰς παρακαταθήκας εὐγνωμονεῖτε
lexical_decisions.chosen: Act honorably with regard to deposits entrusted to you
lexical_decisions.rationale: With entrusted property, εὐγνωμονέω denotes conscientious, fair, or honorable conduct rather than simple gratitude.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τοῦ νῦν μόνου μακροθύμου καὶ ἀγαθοῦ
lexical_decisions.chosen: who only for now is patient and good
lexical_decisions.rationale: This takes μόνου as limiting the present period: God is now patient and good before the appointed judgment. The syntax can alternatively be read as saying that God alone is now patient and good.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τῶν ἀπορρήτων ἀγαθῶν ... ἀπορρήτου κολάσεως
lexical_decisions.chosen: the inexpressible good things ... inexpressible punishment
lexical_decisions.rationale: The repeated adjective ἀπόρρητος is rendered consistently on both sides of the contrast.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἀιδίως ... τὸν αἰῶνα
lexical_decisions.chosen: everlastingly ... throughout the age
lexical_decisions.rationale: The translation preserves the source’s shift from the adverb ἀιδίως to the temporal accusative τὸν αἰῶνα, which may also function idiomatically as “forever.”

source_issues.issue: The supplied print joins the article and noun without a space. This is an orthographic word-division feature and does not create substantive uncertainty.

source_issues.source_quote: ἵνα οἱ ἀγαθοὶ τοῦ λοιποῦ τῶν ἀπορρήτων ἀγαθῶν ἀιδίως ἀπολαύσωσιν, οἱ δὲ ἁμαρτωλοὶ εὑρεθέντες ὡς κακοὶ ἀπορρήτου κολάσεως τεύξονται τὸν αἰῶνα
source_issues.issue: Within the result clause introduced by ἵνα, the first outcome uses the subjunctive ἀπολαύσωσιν, while the second shifts to the future indicative τεύξονται. The translation treats them as coordinated outcomes without correcting the grammatical shift.
